ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle ABCD, point E is the midpoint of CD, point F is a point on BC, and FC = 2BF. Connect AE, EF, and AF. If AB = 2 and AD = 3, what is the measure of $\angle AEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, and AD = 3, AB = 2, \\
thus $\angle B = \angle C = 90^\circ$, CD = AB = 2, BC = AD = 3.\\
Since point E is the midpoint of CD, and FC = 2BF, \\
thus CE = DE = 1, BF = 1, CF = 2.\\
Thus AB = CF = 2, CE = BF = 1.\\
In $\triangle ABF$ and $\triangle FCE$,\\
$\begin{cases} AB=CF\\ \angle B = \angle C\\ BF=CE \end{cases}$, \\
thus $\triangle ABF \cong \triangle FCE$ (by SAS).\\
Thus AF = EF, $\angle BAF = \angle CFE$.\\
Since $\angle B = 90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle BAF + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\angle CFE + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\angle AFE = 180^\circ - (\angle CFE + \angle AFB) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\triangle AFE$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
Thus $\angle AEF = \boxed{45^\circ}$.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个长方形 ABCD，A 在左上角，B 在左下角，C 在右下角，D 在右上角；E 位于右边 CD 上，F 位于底边 BC 上；图中连接了 AE、EF、AF。推理：按照坐标法，令 B=(0,0)，因为 AB=2 且 AB 竖直，所以 A=(0,2)；因为 AD=3 且 AD 水平，所以 C=(3,0)，D=(3,2)。E 是 CD 的中点，所以 E=(3,1)。又 FC=2BF，且 BC=3，所以 BF=1，F=(1,0)。要求 angle AEF，用从 E 出发的向量：EA=A-E=(0,2)-(3,1)=(-3,1)，EF=F-E=(1,0)-(3,1)=(-2,-1)。点积 EA·EF=(-3)(-2)+1(-1)=6-1=5。长度 |EA|=sqrt(9+1)=sqrt(10)，|EF|=sqrt(4+1)=sqrt(5)。因此 cos(angle AEF)=5/(sqrt(10)*sqrt(5))=5/sqrt(50)=1/sqrt(2)，所以 angle AEF=45°。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle ABCD, point E is the midpoint of CD, point F is a point on BC, and FC = 2BF. Connect AE, EF, and AF. If AB = 2 and AD = 3, what is the measure of $\angle AEF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, and AD = 3, AB = 2, \\
thus $\angle B = \angle C = 90^\circ$, CD = AB = 2, BC = AD = 3.\\
Since point E is the midpoint of CD, and FC = 2BF, \\
thus CE = DE = 1, BF = 1, CF = 2.\\
Thus AB = CF = 2, CE = BF = 1.\\
In $\triangle ABF$ and $\triangle FCE$,\\
$\begin{cases} AB=CF\\ \angle B = \angle C\\ BF=CE \end{cases}$, \\
thus $\triangle ABF \cong \triangle FCE$ (by SAS).\\
Thus AF = EF, $\angle BAF = \angle CFE$.\\
Since $\angle B = 90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle BAF + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\angle CFE + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\angle AFE = 180^\circ - (\angle CFE + \angle AFB) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$.\\
Thus $\triangle AFE$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
Thus $\angle AEF = \boxed{45^\circ}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as a rectangle, A is at the upper left corner, B is at the lower left corner, C is at the lower right corner, D is at the upper right corner; E is located on the right side CD; F is located on the bottom side BC; AE, AF, and EF are connected in the figure. Reasoning: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal and adjacent sides are perpendicular, so CD=AB=2, BC=AD=3, and ∠B=∠C=90°. E is the midpoint of CD, therefore CE=DE=1. Also FC=2BF and BC=BF+FC=3, so BF=1, FC=2. Thus AB=FC=2, BF=CE=1, and the included angles ∠B and ∠C are both right angles, so △ABF and △FCE are congruent by SAS. From congruence, AF=EF, and ∠BAF=∠CFE. In right triangle ABF, ∠BAF+∠AFB=90°, so ∠CFE+∠AFB=90°. From the figure it can be seen that B, F, C are collinear, therefore at point F, ∠AFB, ∠AFE, and ∠CFE together form a straight angle, so ∠AFE=180°-90°=90°. Also AF=EF, so △AFE is an isosceles right triangle, and the base angle ∠AEF=45°.
